910.name: Prehistoric Philippines and Early Migrations
910.description: The deep prehistory of the Philippine archipelago from the Callao Man hominin remains, the arrival of Negritos, Austronesian migrations, and the development of diverse linguistic and cultural groups.

sub_clusters.name: Callao Man and Early Humans
sub_clusters.description: The discovery of Homo luzonensis at Callao Cave, the Tabon Man remains in Palawan, Negrito migration across land bridges, and the earliest evidence of human habitation in the Philippines.
key_events: Homo luzonensis discovered at Callao Cave — a distinct hominin species (dated c. 67,000 years ago)

sub_clusters.name: Austronesian Settlement
sub_clusters.description: The Austronesian expansion into the Philippines from Taiwan, the development of rice terracing, seafaring traditions, and the establishment of diverse barangay communities.

910.name: Barangay Era and Maritime Trade
910.description: The barangay polities as the basic political unit, extensive maritime trade networks with China, India, and Southeast Asia, the emergence of Indianized polities, and Islamic influence in the south.

sub_clusters.name: Thalassocratic Polities and Trade Networks
sub_clusters.description: Coastal barangay communities engaging in trade with China, the Sa Huynh-Kalanay interaction sphere, the Laguna Copperplate Inscription, and the development of complex chiefdoms.
key_events: Laguna Copperplate Inscription — oldest known written document in the Philippines (900 AD)

sub_clusters.name: Rajahnates and Islamization
sub_clusters.description: The Rajahnate of Cebu, the Kingdom of Tondo, the arrival of Islam and the establishment of the Sultanate of Sulu and the Sultanate of Maguindanao, Chinese and Malay trade contacts.
key_events: Sultanate of Sulu established as the first Islamic state in the Philippines (c. 1405)
Rajah Humabon of Cebu and the Code of Kalantiaw (traditional dating)

920.name: Spanish Colonization — Early Period
920.description: Magellan's arrival, the establishment of Spanish colonial rule from Mexico via the Manila Galleon trade, the Christianization of the lowlands, and the failed attempts to conquer the Muslim south.

sub_clusters.name: Magellan and Spanish Conquest
sub_clusters.description: Magellan's arrival and death at the Battle of Mactan, Legazpi's establishment of the colonial capital at Manila, the encomienda system, and the beginning of the Manila-Acapulco Galleon trade.
key_events: Ferdinand Magellan killed by Lapulapu at the Battle of Mactan (27 April 1521)
Miguel López de Legazpi establishes Manila as the colonial capital (1571)

sub_clusters.name: Galleon Trade and Christianization
sub_clusters.description: The Manila Galleon trade linking Asia to the Americas, the massive Christianization campaign, the friar estates, the Moro Wars against the Muslim south, and the Chinese sangley community.
key_events: Manila-Acapulco Galleon trade operates for 250 years (1565–1815)
Chinese Sangley uprising in Manila brutally suppressed (1603)

930.name: Late Spanish Period and Philippine Revolution
930.description: The British interlude, the opening of Manila to world trade, the rise of the ilustrado class, José Rizal, the Katipunan, and the Philippine Revolution — the first Asian anti-colonial revolution.

sub_clusters.name: Reform and Ilustrado Movement
sub_clusters.description: The British occupation of Manila, the opening of Philippine ports, the rise of the educated ilustrado class, the Propaganda Movement, José Rizal's Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo.
key_events: José Rizal publishes Noli Me Tangere, galvanizing the reform movement (1887)

sub_clusters.name: Katipunan and Revolution
sub_clusters.description: Andrés Bonifacio's founding of the Katipunan, the Cry of Pugad Lawin, the Revolution against Spain, Rizal's execution, the Aguinaldo-Bonifacio rivalry, and the Declaration of Independence.
key_events: Execution of José Rizal by the Spanish ignites the revolution (30 December 1896)
Emilio Aguinaldo declares Philippine independence at Kawit, Cavite (12 June 1898)

930.name: Philippine-American War and Colonial Period
930.description: The Spanish-American War's transfer of the Philippines to the US, the brutal Philippine-American War, the establishment of American colonial rule, and the Commonwealth period.

sub_clusters.name: Philippine-American War
sub_clusters.description: The Treaty of Paris ceding the Philippines to the US, the eruption of the Philippine-American War, the guerrilla campaign, American atrocities, and the pacification of the Moro Province.
key_events: Philippine-American War erupts; estimated 200,000–1,000,000 Filipino civilian deaths (1899–1902)
Battle of Bud Dajo — US forces massacre Moro villagers in Sulu (1906)

sub_clusters.name: American Colonial Rule and Commonwealth
sub_clusters.description: The 'Benevolent Assimilation' policy, the public education system, the Filipinization of government, the Tydings-McDuffie Act, and the establishment of the Philippine Commonwealth under Quezon.
key_events: Philippine Commonwealth established with Manuel Quezon as president (1935)

940.name: World War II and Japanese Occupation
940.description: The Japanese invasion, the Fall of Bataan and Corregidor, the Death March, Japanese occupation, the guerrilla resistance, MacArthur's return, and the devastating Battle of Manila.

sub_clusters.name: Fall of Bataan and Japanese Occupation
sub_clusters.description: The Japanese invasion, the defense of Bataan and Corregidor, the infamous Bataan Death March, the puppet republic under Laurel, and the Filipino guerrilla resistance movement.
key_events: Bataan Death March — thousands of Filipino and American POWs die (April 1942)
MacArthur's famous pledge: 'I shall return' (March 1942)

sub_clusters.name: Liberation and Independence
sub_clusters.description: MacArthur's return at Leyte, the Battle of Leyte Gulf (largest naval battle in history), the devastating Battle of Manila, and the granting of full independence on July 4, 1946.
key_events: Battle of Leyte Gulf — largest naval battle in history (October 1944)
Battle of Manila devastates the capital; over 100,000 Filipino civilians killed (February–March 1945)
Philippines achieves full independence from the United States (4 July 1946)

950.name: Post-Independence and Marcos Era
950.description: The post-war republic, the Huk Rebellion, Ferdinand Marcos' rise to power, Martial Law, crony capitalism, the Moro insurgency, and the assassination of Ninoy Aquino.

sub_clusters.name: Early Republic and Huk Rebellion
sub_clusters.description: Post-war reconstruction, the Huk Rebellion and Magsaysay's counterinsurgency, the Bell Trade Act, the parity amendment, and the democratic consolidation of the Third Republic.
key_events: Huk Rebellion — communist-led agrarian insurgency in Central Luzon (1946–1954)

sub_clusters.name: Marcos and Martial Law
sub_clusters.description: Ferdinand Marcos' presidency and declaration of Martial Law, the New Society, crony capitalism, human rights abuses, the Moro National Liberation Front, and the assassination of Benigno 'Ninoy' Aquino Jr.
key_events: Marcos declares Martial Law (21 September 1972)
Benigno 'Ninoy' Aquino Jr. assassinated at Manila airport (21 August 1983)

950.name: People Power Revolution
950.description: The peaceful EDSA People Power Revolution that toppled the Marcos dictatorship and installed Corazon Aquino — a landmark moment in global democratic movements.

sub_clusters.name: EDSA People Power Revolution
sub_clusters.description: The snap election, the military defection of Ramos and Enrile, the millions of civilians on EDSA, the fall of the Marcos regime, and the inauguration of Corazon Aquino as president.
key_events: EDSA People Power Revolution — millions take to the streets; Marcos flees to Hawaii (22–25 February 1986)
Corazon Aquino inaugurated as the first female president of the Philippines

960.name: Post-EDSA Democracy
960.description: The restored democracy under the 1987 Constitution, coup attempts, the Ramos economic reforms, EDSA II and III, the Arroyo controversies, and the Aquino III governance reforms.

sub_clusters.name: Aquino and Ramos Era
sub_clusters.description: The Aquino government's democratic restoration, multiple coup attempts, the 1991 Pinatubo eruption, the closure of US military bases, and Ramos' economic liberalization and peace agreements.
key_events: Mount Pinatubo erupts — one of the largest volcanic eruptions of the 20th century (June 1991)
US forces withdraw from Subic Bay and Clark Air Base (1992)

sub_clusters.name: Estrada, Arroyo, and EDSA II
sub_clusters.description: The Estrada presidency and corruption scandals, EDSA II people power ousting Estrada, the controversial Arroyo presidency, the Maguindanao massacre, and the persistent challenges to democratic governance.

sub_clusters.name: Aquino III and Governance Reforms
sub_clusters.description: Benigno Aquino III's anti-corruption agenda, the Bangsamoro peace process, the Mamasapano clash, the Haiyan super typhoon, and the South China Sea arbitration victory.
key_events: Super Typhoon Haiyan (Yolanda) devastates the Visayas, killing over 6,000 (November 2013)
Permanent Court of Arbitration rules in the Philippines' favor on the South China Sea (July 2016)

960.name: Duterte Era and Contemporary Philippines
960.description: Rodrigo Duterte's controversial drug war, the Marawi siege, the pivot toward China, the Marcos Jr. return to power, and the West Philippine Sea confrontations.

sub_clusters.name: Duterte Presidency
sub_clusters.description: Duterte's brutal war on drugs killing thousands, the Marawi siege by ISIS-linked militants, the pivot away from the US toward China, the closure of Boracay, and pandemic governance.
key_events: Duterte's drug war results in thousands of extrajudicial killings (2016–2022)
Battle of Marawi — five-month siege against ISIS-affiliated militants devastates the city (May–October 2017)

sub_clusters.name: Marcos Jr. Presidency
sub_clusters.description: Ferdinand 'Bongbong' Marcos Jr.'s election marking the Marcos family's return to Malacañang, the realignment toward the US, South China Sea tensions, and the ICC investigation of Duterte's drug war.
key_events: Bongbong Marcos wins presidency — the Marcos family returns to power (May 2022)
Escalating confrontations with Chinese vessels in the West Philippine Sea (2023–2025)

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
